data.long_meaning: Derived from the Urdu word ‘imtiaz’, meaning ‘pure’, ‘chaste’, ‘innocent’. The name Imtiazat is often given to girls to signify the purity and innocence of the newborn. The name Imtiazat carries the meaning “Purity, Innocence” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Imtiazat usually hope their child will grow to embody purity, innocence and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Imtiazat total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

In essence, the name Imtiazat calls us to strive for purity not just in physical terms but also in moral, spiritual, and emotional terms as well.

historical_references.reference: Imtiazat was the name of a powerful Turkish slave general under the Mamluk Sultan Qansuh al-Ghuri. He led the Mamluk forces against the Mongol invasion in 1516 CE.

The name Imtiazat is also mentioned in the Persian poetry of Amir Khusrow, a 13th century poet and musician in the Delhi Sultanate. It is used to describe a divine quality or attribute, often translated as 'distinction' or 'excellence'.
